chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Satan troubles the human being most when he is alone, so do not sleep alone, nor travel alone.

key_terms.تَبِيتَنَّ: You spend the night / You sleep
key_terms.يَهُمُّ: He troubles / He tempts / He engages in inner whispering

ai.seo_question: Why is solitude considered spiritually dangerous in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies solitude as a critical window for Shaytan's intensified whispering, framing the prohibition against sleeping or traveling alone as a preventive measure against spiritual negligence. This ruling is deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence, where physical isolation is often correlated with a weakening of divine awareness (ghaflah), making the individual more susceptible to internal temptations. The guidance underscores the importance of maintaining a state of alertness through companionship or community presence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Satan<sup>la</sup> is the most troublesome with the human being when he was alone, therefore do not sleep alone, nor travel alone’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Satan is the strongest against man when he is alone, thus one must not sleep alone or travel alone.’”
